newsitem.title: USA: America Online to launch service in Japan.
newsitem.headline: America Online to launch service in Japan.

text.p: America Online Inc. said on Tuesday it plans to launch an Internet online service in Japan that uses Japanese content, language and customer services.
The service will be launched April 15.
Steve Case, AOL chairman and chief executive, said the company, already the world's biggest online service, plans to make Japan its largest international market.

"Japan is a huge market opportunity for AOL and we are pursuing it aggressively," he said in a statement announcing the service. "Over the next few years, we plan to make Japan our largest international market."
AOL Japan Inc. is a three-way joint venture among America Online, Mitsui & Co. Ltd and Nihon Keizai Shimbun Inc.

The service will be offered at a monthly fee of 980 yen, or about $8.00, for three hours' use, and 480 yen, or about $4.00, for each additional hour. Members will get a 10-hour free trial in the first month, the company said.
With international subscribers just topping the 600,000 mark, AOL said the Japan launch is part of its strategy to expand its global brand.
Japan has almost half of the total PC market in Asia, with more than eight million computers sold in 1996 and about 5.7 million online service subscribers, AOL said.
In Europe, AOL has almost 500,000 members, and AOL Canada has more than 100,000 members, the company said.
